adaptTo() 2026: 25 talks
By Jack Jin · October 10, 2026 · 16 min read · Includes my 14:43 video

adaptTo() 2026 was three days of AEM talks in Berlin, September 28 to 30. I went through all 25 full talks in a 15-minute video: what the talk is, why you should watch it, and my take. This is the written version, in conference order.
adaptTo() 2026, Berlin, September 28 to 30, 2026. Slot times are Berlin time. Each talk links its page and slides on adapt.to.

adaptTo() is Europe's developer conference for Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), organized by diva-e Conclusion. I was just there for the 2026 edition, its 15th anniversary. It was one of the best conferences I've ever attended. Engineers and researchers from Adobe were there, along with engineers and researchers from all over the world. Katie Phillips from Best Buy and I gave a talk there too.
So I gave each of the 25 full talks about 30 seconds on camera. I left out the lightning talks. For each talk I cover three things:
What the talk is
Why you should watch it
My take
It's meant to help you pick which recordings to watch once they're up. Each take is my own limited understanding from the room. Some of it may be wrong, and a few takes are a little spicy.
Below, every talk has its slot, its speakers, links to its page, slides and moment in the video, and the slide I had on screen while I gave my take.

If you made it this far, thank you. And thank you to all the speakers, and to diva-e Conclusion for organizing adaptTo().
The official talk videos should be on the adapt.to schedule in the next week or so. If you'd rather watch than read, the video at the top covers all 25 in under 15 minutes.

imgs.alt: Slide titled On the Shoulders of Giants: a CX Coworker Headless box with planning, policing, approvals, sandboxing and memory, next to marketplaces of plugins (skill, API and MCP tools) and context, making scoped calls to AEM product services and third-party services.

Slide titled What's next?: skills become policies that travel with the token, MCP capability cards in the Adobe Developer Console, AEM MCP governance controls, and an invitation to talk about custom MCP servers behind the AEM MCP server.
Slide titled Blast Radius, not access control: permissions decide what a person is authorized to do, and the server split decides what a machine is even capable of attempting.
Slide titled Why Signal Quality Matters: use signals independent of request size, namely absolute CPU usage, server load ratio, response time P95 and queue depth.
Slide titled Security: AI landscape: vulnerabilities identified and exploited faster than ever, about 2.3 years in 2018 and hours in 2026, next to a falling line chart from zerodayclock.com.
Slide titled Real results from a customer: 80%+ reduction over 3 iterations, above a bar chart of daily content requests by type that drops over time.

Slide titled Confidently wrong: an AI-generated Dispatcher filter with /smartCache and /autoInvalidate properties, stamped WRONG, next to the words Fluent. Confident. Not real. The caption says those filter properties don't exist.

Slide titled The cost of migrating: how long does an AEM migration really take? Months from start to cutover, 8,000+ findings in one BPA report, and about 30% less time to cutover once automated, 6 months manual versus about 4.2 months with Adobe Skills.

Slide titled The solution: Comparador, a freeware Chrome extension for Chromium, Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi, with screenshots and a list of features: under a minute to install, visual diffing, HTML source diffing, HTTP headers comparison, console logs diffing, metrics comparison and shareable project setups.

Slide titled Conceptually: One Framework, Any Content Process: any trigger (human UI, deterministic, AI trigger) flows through a migrator, an eval step, an orchestrator, a generator and a human step to human oversight, preview publish and final publish, with human governance on the entire flow.
Slide titled Calix Web Platform - Evolution: three screenshots, Calix.com rebuilt in 2024, MyCalix as it was until 2025, and MyCalix refreshed in 2026.
Slide with four labels, AI Cloud Workers, Skills, Harnesses and Models (LLMs), around a small S, A, H, M badge, above three screenshots of migrated websites.

Slide titled The Anatomy of a Plugin: a short tools/plugin/index.js that reads the page context, calls an API and writes back into the document, a da.live config table that registers it, and a note that about 15 lines of JavaScript plus a simple HTML file make a complete plugin, served from the same repo as the site.
Slide titled Bring It Inside: before, authors use a separate AI agent outside the authoring experience; after, AI becomes part of the authoring experience in da.live.

Slide titled Finding the right pages: automated scoring: citabilityScore (content gain from optimization) and agenticTraffic (existing AI-crawler traffic) combine into an automated signal that selects pages for experimentation.

Slide titled The problem in plain words: a website visit, a customer record and a browsing history that are not connected, a Tuesday to Thursday timeline where the marketing email goes out after the customer bought elsewhere, and four questions nobody can answer in time: identity, intent, action and delivery.

Slide titled 2026 Evolution, Ease and Practicality: MCP on top of keyword, semantic, hybrid, prefix, multifield, generative and natural language search, aggregates and analyzers, on an indexing and retrieval engine fed by acquisition, custom and AEM content sources.

Slide titled When the content changes: Correctness. An edited promo teaser experience fragment is used on /home, /products, /sale and hundreds more pages. The cache key is the URL and the invalidation key is the path, but the real dependency is a graph. The safe fallback, a full-site purge, throws every good entry away to catch the stale ones: manual, error-prone and hard to reproduce.
Slide titled Visual Rule Editor: no-code visual authoring, predefined rule types (When, Show, Set Value Of, Validate), managing and reusing rules, and drag and drop building.
Slide titled Simplified Index Management: a NEW badge on index.diff with customizations, the same for Quickstart.

Architecture slide: an Asset Portal UI as the custom frontend, an edge worker and storage on an Adobe-managed edge platform (Cloudflare, Fastly) with identity providers and third-party systems, Edge Delivery Services and Content Hub APIs for delivery, and document authoring and AEM Assets author underneath.
Slide titled Prompt anatomy: a minimal e-commerce prompt example that asks for concise, accurate alt text for consumer goods images, with links to fuller versions of the prompts.

Slide titled This is the room today: a photo of the adaptTo() 2026 audience in the conference hall, credited to Marta Cukierman, with the line: Something has shifted. Slowly, but significantly. And we are glad to be back.
